To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for the M/GI/1 queue with Pareto service times, (1) the FB discipline is optimal in the class of all work-conserving and nonanticipatory scheduling disciplines, and (2) the FB discipline has a lower mean delay than the FCFS discipline.
the FB discipline is optimal in the class Π when the service time distribution belongs to the NBUE class, and that the FB discipline minimizes the average delay for the Pareto distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the impact of designing the scheduling discipline when the service time distribution belongs to the NBUE class?
the following questions: • How does the mean delay depend on the scheduling policy?
the problem of minimizing the mean sojourn time in an M/G/1 system with Pareto type service time distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of the M/G/ 1 queue, the optimal discipline is FB for the NBUE class of service time distributions, whereas the optimal discipline is FCFS in the case of DHR service times.
the mean delay is a very sensitive function of the scheduling discipline, and that there is no single optimal discipline for all distributions.

the mean delay in the M/G1 queue is minimized by FB when the hazard rate is positive and nonincreasing, by FCFS when the hazard rate decreases for large values, and by FCFS or FB when the hazard is positive and decreasing for small values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a characterization of the optimal scheduling discipline in the M/G1 queue with Pareto type service times, see [2].
the FB discipline is optimal in this class, but the FCFS discipline is not necessarily optimal in Π.
for Pareto type service time distributions the optimal scheduling discipline is the FCFS discipline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FB discipline may be far from optimal for nonmonotone hazard rate functions, even for the Pareto type distributions.
the FB and FCFS disciplines may be suboptimal in the case of Pareto type service times, even though the Pareto distribution belongs to the NBUE class.
for the class of distributions for which the service time hazard rate is nonincreasing, the optimal scheduling discipline is the FCFS discipline.
